prompt: run(input) receives {"values": [positive ints]} (at least one) and returns their least common multiple.
run(input) receives {"a": int, "b": int, "m": int >= 1} and returns the sorted list of all x in 0..m-1 with a*x = b (mod m); empty if none.

run(input) receives {"congruences": [[r, m], ...], "low": int, "high": int} with moduli that need not be coprime, and returns how many integers x with low <= x <= high satisfy x = r (mod m) for every pair.

A basket of eggs: grouped g at a time, r eggs are left over, for each [g, r] in {"groups": [[g, r], ...]}. run(input) returns the smallest positive number of eggs that fits every grouping, or null if none.

run(input) receives {"grid": [str, ...], "start": [row, col], "goal": [row, col]} with "." free and "#" walls. Return a shortest path as a list of [row, col] cells from start to goal inclusive, found by breadth-first search trying neighbours in the order up, right, down, left (the first time a cell is reached fixes its predecessor); null if unreachable.

Same robot and rules as a breadth-first shortest path that tries neighbours up, right, down, left: run(input) receives {"grid", "start", "goal"} and returns the path as a string of moves U, D, L, R (empty if start is goal), or null if unreachable.

run(input) receives {"grid": [str, ...], "start", "goal", "battery": int} where "." is free, "#" a wall and "C" a charger. Each move uses 1 charge; the robot starts full and entering a "C" cell refills it to "battery". It cannot move with 0 charge. Return the fewest moves to reach goal, or -1.

A warehouse floor has {"rows": int, "cols": int} cells and {"blocked": [[row, col], ...]} shelves. run(input) also receives "from" and "to" cells and returns the fewest up/down/left/right steps between them avoiding shelves, or -1.

run(input) receives {"expr": str} and returns its tokens as a list of [kind, value]: ["num", int] for a run of digits, ["name", str] for a letter followed by letters, digits or "_", and ["op", char] for any other non-space character; spaces separate tokens and are dropped.

run(input) receives {"expr": str, "vars": {name: int}}: an integer expression with + - * /, parentheses, unary minus, spaces and variable names, and returns its int value (usual precedence, left associative, division truncating toward zero). Do not use eval.

run(input) receives {"lines": [str, ...]}, each "name = expression" in the integer expression language with + - * /, parentheses, unary minus and earlier names (division truncates toward zero). Execute the lines in order and return all variables as an object sorted by name. Do not use eval.

A calculator: run(input) receives {"expressions": [str, ...]} of integer arithmetic with + - * /, parentheses and unary minus, division truncating toward zero, and returns the list of their values. Do not use eval.
